headlines: NEW PROPOSAL URGES NONPROFIT TAX ACCOUNTABILITY DASHBOARD ACROSS FLORIDA
TRACKING NONPROFIT TAX BREAKS IN FLORIDA
SHOULD MIAMI-DADE LEAD A STATEWIDE NONPROFIT TAX DASHBOARD?
draft.article: A new proposal calls for Miami-Dade County to lead a statewide effort tracking tax-exempt organizations across Florida. While local homeowners and small businesses pay annual property taxes, thousands of nonprofit hospitals, universities, and foundations do not. Under the plan, an online public dashboard covering all 67 Florida counties would reveal the exact value of unpaid property taxes, executive salaries, government grants, and community benefits. Existing records from the IRS, the Florida Department of Revenue, and the Lown Institute currently sit scattered across separate offices. The initiative urges state legislators, county property appraisers, and nonprofit leaders to unite these numbers so residents can see the real community return.

Investigators stated that Roddrick Victor encountered a woman he knew at the Heat convenience store before following her to the Brownsville Metrorail station across the street. headlines: MIAMI BEACH APPROVES 150,000-SQUARE-FOOT NOLI DISTRICT ON LINCOLN ROAD
MAJOR REDEVELOPMENT LAUNCHES ON LINCOLN ROAD
HISTORIC SAKS FIFTH AVENUE SITE JOINS NEW PEDESTRIAN DISTRICT
draft.article: The city of Miami Beach has officially approved Comras Co. to move forward on the NoLi District, a 150,000-square-foot pedestrian micro-district at the north end of Lincoln Road. Demolition has started at 723 Lincoln Road to build Via NoLi, an 18-foot-wide passageway that connects Lincoln Road to Lincoln Lane, soon to be renamed NoLi Lane. Led by Michael Comras alongside architects Touzet Studio and Beilinson Gomez Architects, the project converts a service alley into a walkway featuring canopy skylights, ceiling fans, boutique shops, and dining. Work will continue through 2027 across spaces including the 40,000-square-foot original Saks Fifth Avenue building at 701 Lincoln Road.

headlines: VICKI LOPEZ FACES ROB PIPER IN DISTRICT 5 RUNOFF
MIAMI-DADE DISTRICT 5 COMMISSION SEAT ON THE LINE
WHO WILL REPRESENT BRICKELL, SOUTH BEACH AND LITTLE HAVANA?
draft.article:
Miami-Dade voters across District 5 are deciding a runoff race between appointed Commissioner Vicki Lopez, 68, and Marine Corps veteran Rob Piper. The district covers Brickell, Downtown, Little Havana, the Miami River, Mid Beach, The Roads, Silver Bluff, Shenandoah, South Beach, and West Flagler.

Lopez took 42.3 percent of the August primary vote, while Piper secured 29.5 percent. The nonpartisan district includes 88,161 registered voters.

A key campaign debate centers on the Live Local Act. Lopez highlights her work passing the housing law, while Piper advocates repealing or revising developer allowances to protect existing neighborhoods.

draft.article: Hialeah Police Department is putting a seized C8 Corvette Stingray Convertible to work for community outreach across Miami-Dade County. Confiscated during a criminal investigation, the sports car will not chase speeders. Instead, officers will display the vehicle at local parks and public gatherings to promote safe driving habits. The city of over 220,000 residents launched the initiative to combat aggressive driving and speeding. Police Chief George Fuente and Mayor Bryan Calvo emphasized crash prevention and resident safety. While the Corvette engages crowds, Commander Patricia Salgado confirmed officers will patrol streets in five conventional vehicles, focusing on school zones and high-crash neighborhoods.

headlines: HEAT BENCH NIKOLA JOVIC AFTER PLAYING TIME DROPS TO ZERO
NIKOLA JOVIC OUT OF HEAT ROTATION
CAN COACH SPOELSTRA FIND A SPOT FOR NIKOLA JOVIC?
draft.article: Miami Heat forward Nikola Jovic is working through another rotation shakeup after seeing his court time vanish. Following appearances of 24, 13, and six minutes across the team's first three games, the 2022 first-round pick played zero minutes during Monday night's home loss to the Dallas Mavericks. Head coach Erik Spoelstra shifted those minutes to guard Dru Smith to bolster perimeter defense alongside frontcourt leaders Bam Adebayo, Giannis Antetokounmpo, and Bobby Portis. Jovic, who is beginning a four-year, $62.4 million contract extension, remains determined to stay ready. Heading into Wednesday's matchup against the Atlanta Hawks, Spoelstra affirmed that the young forward remains fully in the team's plans.

headlines: DADE COUNTY WAS OFFICIALLY CREATED ON FEBRUARY 4, 1836
THE STORY BEHIND DADE COUNTY IN 1836
REMEMBERING OUR EARLY ROOTS ALONG THE MIAMI RIVER
draft.article:
Dade County officially began on February 4, 1836, establishing the foundational identity of our local area. The county received its name from Major Francis L. Dade and the Miami River.

The year 1836 was also marked by key military construction across the region. Fort Dallas was built during the exact same year to serve as an active military base. That installation functioned as an operational post throughout the Second Seminole War, connecting the earliest days of Dade County to the conflict.
